hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever notice how so many hindu families start everything with ganesha? weddings, new homes, the first day of school.
options: hold onto that. this story is the reason.
then this one’s a nice surprise. listen.
then you’ll love where it comes from.

steps.line: On Mount Kailash, Shiva and Parvati held up one perfect fruit for their two sons, Ganesha and Kartikeya.
“Whoever goes around the whole world first,” they said, “wins it.”

steps.q: Kartikeya flies off on his peacock. Ganesha’s ride is a tiny mouse. What do you think Ganesha does?
o: Races off anyway, as fast as the mouse goes
Asks his brother to share the fruit
steps.why: He doesn’t race at all. He circles his parents. Watch why.

steps.line: Kartikeya leapt onto his peacock and shot off across the sky.
Ganesha looked at his ride, a tiny mouse. Then he stood, and slowly walked around his parents, three times.

steps.q: Ganesha has walked around his parents, not the world. What will he say?
o: “The mouse was too slow to try”
steps.why: His logic wins it: for him, going around his parents was going around everything.

steps.line: “You two are my whole world,” he said. “I’ve been around it.” His parents laughed, and gave him the fruit.

steps.q: Walking around something sacred, keeping it on your right, has a name in Hindu worship. What is it?
steps.why: Pradakshina: circling a temple, a shrine or a holy person clockwise, keeping it to your right. Many Hindus still do it at temples today.

steps.line: And so, before weddings, new homes and first days, Hindus begin with Ganesha.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Ganesha is Vighnaharta, the remover of obstacles. Some old stories add a twist. What is it?
o: He only helps people who ask first
He can also set obstacles in the way
He clears just one obstacle a year
steps.why: He’s also Vighnakarta, the one who sets obstacles before those headed the wrong way. Starting with him means asking for the right road, not just a clear one.

say: here’s what i love. ganesha won without running at all. he just knew what his world was.
that’s why so many hindus begin with him: before the big plans, remember what matters most.

steps.q: The best-known short prayer to Ganesha, “Vakratunda Mahakaya,” asks him to clear obstacles. From which tasks?
o: Only the big ones, like weddings
steps.why: Its last line: nirvighnam kuru me deva, sarva-karyeshu sarvada, “make all my work free of obstacles, always.” Not only weddings: a test, a new job, a long drive.

today.say: before you start something today, a meeting, a workout, a hard conversation, pause for five seconds and ask: what matters most here? you can say om gam ganapataye namah, if you’d like. it’s your choice.
options: five seconds. that’s all ganesha needed.
that’s okay. the question will keep.

tomorrow.line: ganesha’s pen breaks halfway through writing a great epic. what he does next is why his statues look the way they do.
